title: Identifiability and approximation bias in computational inference

items.title: Total variation controls expectations of bounded functions
items.statement: For probability measures P,Q on a measurable space with the library convention d_TV(P,Q)=sup_A |P(A)-Q(A)|, a measurable g with 0<=g<=M satisfies |int g dP-int g dQ|<=M d_TV(P,Q); a measurable real f with |f|<=C satisfies |int f dP-int f dQ|<=2C d_TV(P,Q).

references.title: Alison L. Gibbs and Francis E. Su, On Choosing and Bounding Probability Metrics, International Statistical Review 70(3), 419-435 (2002)
David A. Levin, Yuval Peres, and Elizabeth L. Wilmer, Markov Chains and Mixing Times, 2nd ed., §4.1 and Proposition 4.5

items.title: Exact inferential targets and approximation chains
items.statement: On a fixed observed-data fiber, an explicitly supplied measurable likelihood version with finite positive prior evidence defines a proper exact posterior target by normalization. An approximation target is a separately specified object in the same declared metric space. A finite reference chain in one metric space assigns each adjacent discrepancy to its named statistical or computational stage.

references.title: Anthony Davison and David Hinkley, Bootstrap Methods and Their Application, Chapter 2 §2.5
Jarno Lintusaari, Michael U. Gutmann, Ritabrata Dutta, Samuel Kaski, and Jukka Corander, Fundamentals and Recent Developments in Approximate Bayesian Computation

items.title: Metric approximation error decomposes along a finite reference chain
items.statement: For any finite chain T_0,...,T_m,T_hat in one metric space, m>=0, d(T_0,T_hat)<=sum_{j=1}^m d(T_{j-1},T_j)+d(T_m,T_hat). If T_0 is a scientific reference and T_1 the exact inferential target, the first term is the declared sampling/model discrepancy and subsequent terms are computational discrepancies.

references.title: Anthony Davison and David Hinkley, Bootstrap Methods and Their Application, Chapter 2 §2.5
Alison L. Gibbs and Francis E. Su, On Choosing and Bounding Probability Metrics, International Statistical Review 70(3), 419-435 (2002)

items.title: Gaussian density integrals for supplied length measures
items.statement:
For $d\in\{1,2\}$, suppose a countably additive measure $\lambda_d$ on $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d)$ is supplied and satisfies
$$\lambda_d\!\left(\prod_{j=1}^d(a_j,b_j]\right)=\prod_{j=1}^d(b_j-a_j)\qquad(a_j<b_j).$$
No assertion about constructing these measures is made.

1. If $Q$ is a nondegenerate compact box and $h:Q\to\mathbb R$ is bounded, Borel measurable and Riemann integrable, then its integral against the supplied measure equals its proper Riemann integral. Nonnegative Borel functions on the whole space are computed from increasing compact-box cutoffs by monotone convergence.
2. For the supplied $\lambda_1$, every $m\in\mathbb R$, $v>0$ and
$$g_{m,v}(x)=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi v}}e^{-(x-m)^2/(2v)}$$
satisfy
$$\int g_{m,v}\,d\lambda_1=1,\qquad \int xg_{m,v}(x)\,d\lambda_1(x)=m,\qquad \int(x-m)^2g_{m,v}(x)\,d\lambda_1(x)=v.$$
The signed first moment is absolutely integrable. These are density-integral statements and require no choice axiom in addition to the supplied measures.
items.axiom_use: None beyond the explicitly supplied countably additive Borel measures with their box-volume contract. The proof does not construct Lebesgue measure or a normal probability law.

references.title: John K. Hunter, Measure Theory, Chapter 4; local Darboux comparison and Gaussian calculation under supplied measures

title: Identifiability and approximation bias in computational inference — Examples

items.title: A full-rank local Hessian does not capture both posterior modes
items.statement: An identifiable finite-data model can have an exact posterior proportional to exp(-n(theta^2-1)^2) on [-2,2]. Both equal global modes have full-rank negative Hessian, yet the one-mode Laplace Gaussian based at +1 stays at least asymptotically 1/2 away in total variation from the full posterior.

references.title: Laplace method for integrals, PHYS 2400, University of Connecticut, complete 7-page note
NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §2.3(iii), Laplace's Method
Francis Bach, Approximating Integrals with Laplace's Method

items.title: An optimized mean-field law can lose posterior correlation
items.statement: Optimizing an independent Gaussian mean-field family by the evidence lower bound need not recover the marginal variances or dependence structure of the exact inferential target.

references.title: David M. Blei, Alp Kucukelbir, and Jon D. McAuliffe, Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians, §2.3 and Figure 1
Michael I. Jordan et al., An Introduction to Variational Methods for Graphical Models, §6.3.1
Ronghuo Zheng, Zhiting Hu, and Yuntian Deng, 10-708 Probabilistic Graphical Models, Lecture 13: Variational Inference II, complete 9-page lecture note

items.axiom_use: None beyond the reference length and area measures supplied in the example. Their Borel restrictions satisfy the box-volume contract; finite Darboux bounds, explicit cutoffs, and compact Gaussian integration prove all normalizers and moments without constructing Lebesgue measure or using AC-dependent normal laws.

items.title: A Gaussian synthetic likelihood can change an exact posterior
items.statement: Two identifiable discrete summary laws can have the same mean and positive variance, so the ideal Gaussian synthetic likelihoods agree at every observation even though the exact posterior and synthetic-likelihood posterior differ.

references.title: Victor M.-H. Ong et al., Variational Bayes with Synthetic Likelihood, Statistics and Computing 28(4), 971-988 (2018)
Paul Fearnhead et al., Bayesian Inference Using Synthetic Likelihood: Asymptotics and Adjustments, 2019 arXiv preprint arXiv:1902.04827
Christopher C. Drovandi et al., Approximating the Likelihood in Approximate Bayesian Computation, Handbook of Approximate Bayesian Computation (2020)

items.title: A nonconstant summary can lose an identifiable parameter
items.statement: The full model can identify theta while a nonconstant zero-tolerance ABC summary target remains the prior and differs from the exact posterior.

references.title: Christian P. Robert et al., Lack of Confidence in Approximate Bayesian Computation Model Choice, PDF pp. 1-4
Jarno Lintusaari et al., Fundamentals and Recent Developments in Approximate Bayesian Computation, PDF pp. 1-6, 10-23, 46-47
Paul Fearnhead and Dennis Prangle, Constructing Summary Statistics for Approximate Bayesian Computation: Semi-automatic ABC, PDF pp. 1-18, 35-38
Michael G. B. Blum, Approximate Bayesian Computation: A Nonparametric Perspective, PDF pp. 1-11, 20-24; supplemental Lemma 2 not used

items.title: Positive ABC tolerance changes an identity-summary target
items.statement: With the identity summary and positive prior-predictive acceptance probability, the tolerance $\epsilon=3/5$ gives an ABC target whose mass at $\theta=1$ is $9/17$, while the exact posterior mass is $4/5$; the total-variation distance is exactly $23/85$.

references.title: Jarno Lintusaari et al., Fundamentals and Recent Developments in Approximate Bayesian Computation, PDF pp. 1-6, 10-23, 46-47
Paul Fearnhead and Dennis Prangle, Constructing Summary Statistics for Approximate Bayesian Computation: Semi-automatic ABC, PDF pp. 1-18, 35-38

items.axiom_use: None. All probabilities and tolerance-ball events are finite and explicit; the rejection statement assumes an IID proposal-simulator sequence as stated in its supplier.
